rv.q: In Brigid Larmour’s finely etched production, irritable passions ferment beneath the frowsty knits and beads.
This is a wonderful revival of a marvellous play.
The Old Ladies really is a creaky old piece of theatre.

cn.t: This 1935 psychological thriller divides critics: some find it atmospherically compelling in its portrait of isolated elderly women, while others consider it dated and tame by modern standards.
